items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good YouTube video comparing the GTA 6 game map with real Miami. The Narrator is THRILLED and grinning the whole time: an excited, fun friend who just found out how much Rockstar copied from Miami and is bursting to tell you. Huge smile you can hear in every line, bright and upbeat, warm and natural like real excited conversation, never like reading a script. Wide, lively pitch movement; real amazement on every number and reveal; playful delighted laughter in the voice on the funny bits (the lobster that turned into a whale, the 105 metres). The opening bet is a cheeky, confident challenge with a grin. Punch the key words with energy. Pace quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never flat, calm, sleepy, monotone or documentary-serious, and never shouty or fake. Accent: native General American English, neutral American accent from first word to last. VOICE IDENTITY: the same person and the same high energy from the first line to the last. Say 'GTA six' as the letters G, T, A then 'six'. Pronounce 'Cortez' as 'cor-TEZ', 'Colon' exactly like the punctuation mark 'colon' (KOH-lun), never 'Colonna'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word: stop right after the final sentence and never add, invent or continue with any words of your own.
lines: I bet you a hundred dollars you've already seen the GTA six map. Because Rockstar didn't invent Vice City. They copied it. From Miami. A hotel strip, copied right down to the palm trees. An apartment building that doesn't exist anymore... except in the game. A swamp, a sugar town, a giant lobster that turned into a whale. And mountains, in a state whose highest point is 105 metres. GTA six launches November 19th. So let's put the trailers next to the real map. And at the end, I'll show you the moment Miami started copying the game back. Grab a controller. And a map of Florida. Ten stops. Stop one. Ocean Drive, Miami Beach. Pastel Art Deco hotels, neon signs, palm trees, and the beach right across the road. In the trailers, it's called Ocean Beach. Same strip. Same pastel colours. The Colony Hotel becomes the Cortez. Hotel Victor becomes Hotel Dixon. And here's the thing. Rockstar has copied this street before. In 2002's Vice City, that same Colony Hotel was the "Colon" Hotel. Same building. Copied twice. Twenty-four years apart. That hotel is still standing. But a few blocks away, two towers are slowly going down.
